agree.reason: The $59 trial, the no-contract terms and the meal swaps make it easy for a wary reader to start, but nothing tells someone who has quit three services why this one would last past two months, so the reader may just see a fourth attempt.

honest.reason: The page correctly turns down the 'will lower your A1C' promise and gives the 10/3/1 split, but it leaves out that medication changes weren't tracked, which weakens the A1C figures, and it says the 0.6 average covers 'all 14', which the brief doesn't establish.

works_the_facts.reason: Figures are copied as given instead of worked: it doesn't point out that about 42% of customers have stayed past six months, doesn't give the $12.90-per-meal cost, and doesn't compare the trial's cost per meal.

right_comparison.reason: Cooking for yourself and counting carbs is described briefly and fairly, but the page never sets the service against the apps and delivery plans this reader has already dropped, and that's the comparison the reader is actually making.

qualification.reason: 'Results vary, and we can't promise any result' is a generic hedge with nothing the reader can check; the only conditions with a date are the Thursday-noon order deadline and the 25-mile delivery range.

objections.reason: Swaps, the 4-week menu rotation and cancel-any-time address boredom and lock-in, but the page leaves out the 15-minute call with Lena and never links the 37 long-term customers to the reader's worry about quitting again.

fit.reason: It is a clearly organised sales page of about 430 words with a single order button, close to the length and form the brief asked for.
